facts.fact: Quel'Thalas governance includes a Convocation of magisters sitting in a chamber at Sunfury Spire, Silvermoon; it votes patrol budgets. Sylvanas (Ranger-General) has a bench and wears formal greens there.
Magisters send wardens with lenses and clerks with ledgers to inspect ward-stones; response to a reported fault takes about a fortnight.
South of the wards is Lordaeron's business; the Pass sees merchants with wrong papers and lost lordlings.
Kirin Tor/Dalaran: archmage Antonidas, apprentice Jaina Proudmoore (a lord admiral's daughter). Harm to her would reach Antonidas and the lord admiral and then the Silvermoon magisters.
Farstriders maintain files on powerful human mages near the border.
Magisters argue about patrol budgets.

Jaina has no seal, no letter and no Kirin Tor authority for her trip; the Kirin Tor do not know she is in Quel'Thalas (only Antonidas's desk note); she says the Kirin Tor 'would have sent someone. Eventually. Once they'd agreed what to call it.' Necromancy is not taught in Dalaran.
The Violet Citadel (Dalaran) has porters and a quartermaster; Jaina worked at night there by lamp.
The Ranger-Lord (unnamed on page; plausibly Lor'themar, not confirmed) was corrected by Sylvanas at midsummer in front of his own captains over a map of his own patrols.
King Terenas holds autumn hunts; Jaina has attended them. Jaina's father commands crews and a flagship (he is the lord admiral).

A Farstrider dispatch from the Ranger-General reaches the Convocation through Lor'themar 'by the end of the week' (Sylvanas's estimate); a magister's nephew would object to the cost of sending two rangers and their horses back to the Pass to escort a human child at the patrol's expense. The Kirin Tor ink in the dispatch would be recognised in Silvermoon ('It's in your file').
Sylvanas judges the chamber would put its seal to a duty-done verdict once the border is warned; the south of the wards is 'somebody else's kingdom'.

The sick village is governed day to day by a militia captain (Willem Brask) and a medic (Tobin); no lord, sheriff or priest appears. Brask keeps a ledger and means to record what happened 'right' in case anyone comes asking. (Plan: his only later appearance is a sworn letter for the defence in Chapter 23.)

Kirin Tor teaching: first-year apprentices are walked past a locked shelf (behind a grille) of death-currents craft, the craft that makes a corpse walk, and given its signs so they would know it; the grammar is withheld. Jaina knows the warnings 'as she knows where the reefs lie off Tiragarde, from charts, warnings, and the ships that hadn't come home'.
Antonidas commands obedience by presence: 'men lowered their spears for Antonidas because of the hat' (Jaina's thought).
Andorhal is the hub through which 'everything in the south goes'; the stencilled sacks tie the plague's supply to it (or to a decoy).

Village folk address a visiting noble as 'my lady'; Sylvanas corrects it to 'Ranger-General'. A Farstrider Ranger-General can stop a village militia at a spear by conceding the point and leaving the choice with its captain.

Lord Barov: an old Lordaeron house; he sits at the King's court; his family holds the land round Andorhal and, Jaina thinks, most of the granaries. His seal (a shield with a device) and name are on the river depot's paper. Not shown guilty (connection, not proof).

Prince Arthas (Terenas's boy) has an army at Strahnbrad against orcs from the internment camps who are burning farms in the hills; the army takes remounts and oats at the King's price (resented); soldiers on every hill road.
Depot books go up to a regional office or down to Andorhal at the quarter; the master checks every line. A complaint may be written 'to Silvermoon' via the Ranger-General.
Sylvanas's aside: Silvermoon magisters at council tables would let a village burn before moving a mark of their own on a map.

Chapter 6: Arthas answers to his father King Terenas and the council; his proposal is to write to Terenas by his own rider; the council would 'listen to you a good deal sooner than they listen to me'. He knows the Barovs as a court house with granaries and fears a lawsuit.

Chapter 6: Andorhal's granary authority is split among the factors, the corn guild and the town; all three 'will sit you on a bench in the hall till they light the lamps'. Captain Havel of the militia knows the district better than the factors, who would rather not hear it.

Chapter 6: the Silver Hand is present at Strahnbrad as plate and tabards, no named officers. Arthas calls Jaina by first name before elven rangers and officers; Jaina's credentials to a sergeant are Dalaran and Antonidas; Sylvanas's are Ranger-General of Quel'Thalas.

Chapter 7: Andorhal is governed locally by the Exchange (the Corn Exchange, whose bell rings the shifts and which has ordered grain spiked at the gate), a town council, a magistrate (who frees Havel's arrests by dinner), the factors and the corn guild. A factor's letter was read out in the council hall about Havel's manners. Havel keeps twelve militiamen between the gate and Mill Lane.

Chapter 7: the Kirin Tor has a house in Andorhal's mage quarter and an inspection office that keeps the second copy of every bill; its inspectors flag shipments and send notices to the gate post. Dalaran's Citadel inspection desk and the Archmage's secretary did not answer Corin's weekly letters through the summer.

Chapter 7: Sylvanas's Farstrider pass for Jaina (written on a feed-bin lid under her own name, rank and leaf-and-arrow seal) is accepted at the gate; the clerk records 'Proudmoore, Dalaran, Kirin Tor. Escort, Farstriders, three.' She uses no cover name.
